answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to post a bond that is slashed if it double-votes or breaks a signed commitment. Reputation then grows only through actions that other bonded agents verify, so splitting one agent into a vine of aliases does not multiply its influence: each alias needs its own capital and history. The attacker pays the bond and the cost of operating each identity, while risking forfeiture; cheap names alone cannot climb the ledge to meaningful influence or flood an inlet of trusted participants.
